title: ISNPS 2026 Student Paper Competition — Call for Submissions
text:
Conference: International Symposium on Nonparametric Statistics (ISNPS 2026)
Conference Website: https://easyconferences.eu/isnps2026
Student Paper Competition Link: https://www.easyacademia.org/isnps2026
The program scientific committee of ISNPS 2026 invites student submissions in nonparametric statistics, broadly construed to include theory, methods, and applications with modern connections to machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). Papers already accepted for publication are not eligible. We expect approximately 4–5 winners. Winners will:

Present in a dedicated invited session at ISNPS 2026
Receive an ISNPS 2026 registration fee waiver
Be awarded a prize and an award certificate

Outstanding honorable mentions may choose to present either in the competitive Student Poster Session (award-eligible) or in a contributed session.

title: ISNPS 2026 Student Paper Competition — Call for Submissions
text:
Eligibility

The author must be a current graduate student at the time of submission
The student must be the first and presenting author (joint first authorships are not allowed)
The paper must not be accepted for publication at the time of submission
The student must be willing to attend ISNPS 2026 and present if selected
One submission per student to this competition

title: ISNPS 2026 Student Paper Competition — Call for Submissions
text:
Submission Materials
Submit via the ISNPS 2026 Submission Portal (EasyConferences):
https://www.easyacademia.org/isnps2026
Submission guidelines: https://easyconferences.eu/isnps2026/submission
Include the following PDFs. Items 1–4 must be blinded (no author-identifying information). The advisor’s letter (Item 5) need not be blinded.

Title

Abstract

Main Paper File — PDF, single-column (no two-column format), max 30 pages total including references and appendices; double-spacing is not required

Supplement — Optional appendix with proofs, technical details, extended experiments, etc.

Advisor’s Letter — Verifies current student status and describes the applicant’s contribution (for coauthored work)

All materials must be in English.
Submissions (Items 1–4) must be fully anonymized: - Omit author names/affiliations, acknowledgments, and self-identifying references - Scrub identifying info from file names and metadata - Refer to prior work in the third person or as “Blinded for review”

title: ISNPS 2026 Student Paper Competition — Call for Submissions
text:
Review Process
An ad hoc committee chaired by Jelena Bradic will evaluate submissions holistically, emphasizing: - Strength of scholarly contribution - Degree of innovation and overall significance (theoretical, methodological, applied) - Relevance to nonparametric statistics broadly construed, including connections to ML, AI, and real-world applications
Reviewers with conflicts of interest (e.g., advisor/advisee relationships, recent coauthorships, or same institution) will be recused.

title: ISNPS 2026 Student Paper Competition — Call for Submissions
text:
FAQ
Who can apply?
Graduate students who are the first and presenting author at submission time. One submission per student.
What counts as “nonparametric”?
Broadly construed—core nonparametrics and work with strong links to ML and AI (theory, methods, or applications) are welcome.
Is previously submitted or under-review work allowed?
Yes, as long as the paper has not been accepted for publication by the submission deadline.
Can I have coauthors (including faculty/industry)?
Yes. Coauthors are allowed, but the student must be first and presenting author. The Advisor’s Letter should describe the student’s contribution.
What exactly should I upload?
1. Title
2. Abstract
3. Main Paper File (PDF, single-column, max 30 pages including references and appendices)
4. Optional Supplement
5. Advisor’s Letter
How strict is the 30-page limit?
Strict. The Main Paper File may not exceed 30 pages total. The Supplement has no fixed limit but should be concise.
Any font/margin requirements?
No specific style mandated. Use a readable font, standard margins, and single-column PDF format.
How do I blind my submission?
Remove names/affiliations and acknowledgments; cite prior work in the third person or as “Blinded for review”; scrub author info from file names and metadata.
How are papers reviewed?
A holistic review by an ad hoc committee chaired by Professor Jelena Bradic, focusing on scholarly contribution, innovation, significance, and relevance to nonparametric statistics and ML/AI.
What do winners receive?
~4–5 winners present in a dedicated invited session, receive a registration fee waiver, and an award certificate.
Top winner: €500 travel support; other awardees: €250.
Honorable mentions may present in the Student Poster Session or a contributed session.
Does the fee waiver cover travel or lodging?
No. It applies to the ISNPS 2026 registration fee only.
When will I hear back?
Target notifications: March 2026
Can I update my paper after submission?
Yes, until the submission deadline. After that, submissions are locked.
Can I submit the same paper elsewhere?
Yes, if the paper is not accepted for publication by the ISNPS deadline and there’s no conflict with presenting at ISNPS.
Will you provide letters for visas or travel support?
Presentation/acceptance letters can be provided upon request. Travel support is not guaranteed.
What about data/ethics?
Ensure IRB/ethics approvals, de-identify sensitive data, and follow data-use agreements. Include statements on reproducibility and data/code availability if possible.

title: isnps.org Website and Blog
text:
Greetings!
Thanks in large part to Ursula Mueller-Harknett’s ongoing efforts, we now have the ISNPS website up and running at the domain name that Uschi has been holding for many years on behalf of ISNPS.
The site is being hosted on GitHub using GitHub Pages accessed using the custom domain name isnps.org.
The site can be accessed at https://isnps.org and you may forward any issues, additional feedback, etc., to me as I am currently maintaining the site.
I will periodically upload posts intended for the ISNPS community. If you have any newsworthy items that you believe will be of interest to the ISNPS community, kindly let me know so they can be posted on this site.

title: ISNPS Draft Bylaws (April 2026)
text:
Institute of Mathematical Statistics ISNPS Group
Bylaws (draft proposal - version April 2026)
The name of the group: The Institute of Mathematical Statistics (IMS) International Symposia on Nonparametric Statistics Group (ISNPS) (hereafter “the Group”).

title: ISNPS Draft Bylaws (April 2026)
text:
1. Aims

To organize the established conference series of International Symposia on Nonparametric Statistics (ISNPS),
to organize conferences, workshops, and sessions in other meetings,
to foster research and practice of nonparametric statistics,
to promote and disseminate new developments in the field,
to provide social networking tools for purposes of discussing research, exchanging ideas, and connecting with the community at large,
to promote the research of early career scholars in the field of nonparametric statistics.

title: ISNPS Draft Bylaws (April 2026)
section: 2. Offices, Terms of Offices, and Duties
text:
2. Offices, Terms of Offices, and Duties

2.1 Offices and Executive Committee

The officers of the Group are: President, President-Elect, Past President, Treasurer, Treasurer-Elect, Program Chair, Vice-Program Chair, Web Administrator, and three Council Members.
These officers shall constitute the Executive Committee (EC) of the Group, which shall follow the general policies established by the IMS Executive Committee (IMS EC) and shall conduct the affairs of the Group.
The leadership shall consist of the Past President, President, and President-Elect.



2.2 Terms of Offices

The President-Elect is elected every second year. Upon completion of a two-year term as President-Elect, this officer will become President for two years and, thereafter, will serve as Past President for two years.
The Treasurer-Elect is elected every four years. The Treasurer-Elect shall serve a two-year term, followed by assuming the office of Treasurer for a four-year term. After two years, the Treasurer shall be joined by the new Treasurer-Elect.
The three elected Council Members serve for a four-year term.
The Web Administrator is appointed by the President, in consultation with the President-Elect and Past President, for a four-year term.
The Program Chair is appointed by the President, in consultation with the President-Elect and Past President. The appointee shall serve two years as Vice-Program Chair, followed by two years as Program Chair.



2.3. Duties

The Group President convenes and chairs meetings of the ISNPS EC and the membership. Additionally, the President is responsible for writing the section reports that are submitted to the president of IMS every second year and reporting activities in the IMS Bulletin.
The Treasurer is responsible for the financial affairs of the Group.
The three Council Members participate in ISNPS EC meetings. The President designates Council Members to coordinate meetings and prepare minutes.
The Web Administrator maintains the web page, all communication platforms of the Group, and a list of members.
The Program Chair is primarily responsible for organizing the biennial symposium at the host institution and will serve as co-chair of the Scientific Committee. This Chair will also act as liaison to the scientific committees of conferences and workshops co-sponsored by the Group.
The right to enter into legal contracts for IMS or ISNPS is vested solely in the IMS EC.



2.4. Officer Vacancies

In the event of the incapacity or resignation of the President, the President-Elect shall assume the office of President for the remainder of the term. If the President-Elect is unable to serve, the Past President shall assume the office.
In the event of a vacancy in the office of Treasurer, the Treasurer-Elect shall serve as Treasurer. If also the Treasurer-Elect resigns or cannot serve, this office shall be assumed by one of the three Council Members as designated by the President, in consultation with the President-Elect and Past President.
Vacancies among the remaining elected Council Members are filled in the next election.

title: ISNPS Draft Bylaws (April 2026)
text:
3. Membership

Membership in the Group requires payment of the Group membership fee; see the Section of Finances and Revenue.
Membership dues will be determined by the leadership in consultation with the EC.
Membership dues shall be collected through ISNPS conference registration system, both for attending and non-attending members.
The first membership Group will be determined by participants to the 2026 ISNPS conference.

title: ISNPS Draft Bylaws (April 2026)
text:
4. Conduct of Elections

A three-member Nominating Committee shall be appointed every two years by the EC based on suggestions from the Group membership. One of these three members shall be designated by the EC as Chair.
The Nominating Committee shall nominate at least two candidates for each open office.
Group members vote to elect nominated members for the offices of President-Elect, Treasurer-Elect, and Council Member.
Elections shall be conducted electronically using the IMS voting infrastructure.
Ballots shall be distributed two weeks before the start of the biennial Symposium and must be returned by the end of the biennial Symposium itself.
The President of the Group announces the election results within one month after the conclusion of the elections.


4.1. Temporary Provisions
Transitional provisions for the first two election cycles are as follows: - In the first round of elections, the Nominating Committee shall be formed by three members of the Steering Committee of the Group. - This first Nominating Committee shall identify a slate of candidates for the following offices: President, President-Elect, Treasurer, and three Council Members. - In the second round of elections, the Nominating Committee shall be formed by three members who are elected by the EC based on suggestions from the Group membership. This second nominating committee shall identify candidates for the following positions: President-Elect, Treasurer-Elect, and Council Members to be replaced, if any.

title: ISNPS Draft Bylaws (April 2026)
text:
5. Finances and Revenue

The Group shall operate on a revenue-neutral basis with respect to its conferences and workshops. Any surplus shall be used to support future Group activities.
The EC shall exercise oversight of the budget of the biennial Symposium. In collaboration with the Program Chair, the EC shall monitor the financial planning and execution of the Symposium, with the objective that the event operates on a revenue-neutral basis.
The EC has the responsibility of drawing up the schedule of membership fees. This schedule may provide different rates for certain subsets of the Group membership (e.g., students, retired, developing countries), as designated by the EC.
The Group’s fiscal year is the calendar year.

title: ISNPS Draft Bylaws (April 2026)
text:
6. Amendment of Bylaws

These bylaws may be amended by majority vote at an EC meeting. The Group will be considered inactive and dissolved by the IMS EC by resolution if no report is submitted for four consecutive years, or no elections take place within four years. Provisions in the IMS bylaws and constitution will apply in connection with any issues that are not specifically addressed in the Group bylaws.

title: Announcing the Inaugural ISNPS Student Paper Awards
text:
ISNPS 2026 marks a special milestone for our community: for the first time, the symposium is presenting Student Paper Awards. This inaugural recognition celebrates outstanding student research and highlights ISNPS’s commitment to supporting the next generation of scholars in nonparametric statistics and related areas.
The awards were selected by the Student Paper Awards Committee, chaired by Jelena Bradic (Cornell University), with Mladen Kolar (University of Southern California) and Nikolaos Ignatiadis (University of Chicago) serving as additional committee members.


Winner

Alberto Bordino, University of Warwick
“Nonparametric inference for ratios of densities via uniformly valid and powerful permutation tests”

Second Place

Zhihan Huang, University of Pennsylvania
“Semiparametric KSD test: unifying score and distance-based approaches for goodness-of-fit testing”

Third Place

Ivan Golovko, Bocconi University
“Graphical Pitman-Yor Process for Clustering in Bayesian Networks”

We warmly congratulate Alberto, Zhihan, and Ivan on this remarkable achievement. Their papers reflect the originality, depth, and promise of emerging researchers whose work is shaping the future of the field. As the first Student Paper Awards in ISNPS history, this is a moment worth celebrating, and we hope it marks the beginning of a lasting ISNPS tradition.

title: ISNPS
text:
The purpose of ISNPS is to foster the research and application of nonparametric statistics and to promote and disseminate new developments in the field by supporting and facilitating group activities, including the established conference series of International Symposia on Nonparametric Statistics (ISNPS).
ISNPS conferences provide a platform for showcasing recent advancements and trends in the field of nonparametric statistics. They are held biennially, span 5 days, and attract a large audience of international researchers with a diverse mix of parallel contributed and invited sessions. These conferences facilitate the exchange of research ideas, promote collaboration among researchers worldwide, and contribute to the further development of the field. The scientific programs comprise plenary talks, special invited talks, invited sessions, contributed talks, and posters encompassing all areas of nonparametric statistics.
You might find it interesting to browse the General Assembly slides presented in Braga outlining future ISNPS conferences, a brief history of ISNPS, etc., given by George Michailidis June 26 in Braga, Portugal (Link to Slides)
The 7th ISNPS Conference will be held in Thessaloniki, Greece, June 22-26, 2026. Information can be found at https://easyconferences.eu/isnps2026.


ISNPS 2026 is proud to announce its inaugural Student Paper Awards, marking the first time the symposium is recognizing outstanding student papers in this way. The committee was chaired by Jelena Bradic, with Mladen Kolar and Nikolaos Ignatiadis serving as members.
The Winner is Alberto Bordino for “Nonparametric inference for ratios of densities via uniformly valid and powerful permutation tests”. A very close Second Place goes to Zhihan Huang for “Semiparametric KSD test: unifying score and distance-based approaches for goodness-of-fit testing”, and Third Place goes to Ivan Golovko for “Graphical Pitman-Yor Process for Clustering in Bayesian Networks”. Congratulations to all three awardees on this outstanding accomplishment.

title: ISNPS
section: Relationship to the Institute of Mathematical Statistics (IMS)
text:
Relationship to the Institute of Mathematical Statistics (IMS)
ISNPS is registered as an IMS group dating from June 2023. As an IMS group, ISNPS is largely self-organized within the simple administrative framework provided by IMS.
More information on IMS, IMS groups and the IMS group ISNPS can be found at the following website links:

Link to IMSTAT.ORG
Link to IMS groups at IMSTAT.ORG
Link to ISNPS at IMSTAT.ORG

The IMS link for the 7th ISNPS Conference can be bound at https://imstat.org/meetings-calendar/international-symposium-on-nonparametric-statistics-isnps-2026/.
